the identification and characterization of the enzymes involved in the digestive process of crustaceans, and how they contribute to the nutritional value of crustacean food.
the characterization of peptidases and other enzymes in lobster gastric juice.
the identification, functional characterization and comparative analysis of digestive enzymes in crustaceans, and the development of new tools to study their activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proteomic analysis of gastric juice from a crustaceans provides a new perspective on the digestive physiology of these animals, and that the zymoMPS approach provides a new tool to characterize the substrate specificity of peptidases.
the digestive peptidase complement in H. americanus has a wide range of substrate specificities and is cold-adapted, which makes them useful for biotechnological applications.

the digestive peptidome of the lobster is a complex system that includes many enzymes with overlapping substrate specificities, which are likely to have evolved to optimize digestion in the variable environmental conditions of the ocean.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the most abundant classes and individual enzymes of the lobster digestive fluid.
we have uncovered the functional role of each individual peptidase in the lobster gastric juice, and we have shown that the substrate specificity of these enzymes is determined by the S2 pocket.
we have identified the major classes of digestive enzymes from a crustaceans, characterized their substrate specificity and compared their enzymatic properties to those of mammalian enzymes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proteomic and biochemical approaches complement each other and can be used to uncover the functional role of individual enzymes in digestion.
the zymoMPS approach is a novel and powerful tool for determining the proteolytic specificity and substrate preferences of individual peptidases from a complex mixture.
the zymoMPS approach is a useful tool to uncover the substrate specificities of multiple enzymes simultaneously and can be applied to any proteolytic system.
